https://www.politico.eu/article/spacex-b.text: PARIS — Four U.S. space companies said they would skip French President Emmanuel Macron’s space summit in Paris next week after coming under pressure from U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration . Elon Musk’s SpaceX, Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin, rocket maker Stoke Space and Starcloud, a startup that is trying to launch data centers in space, notified French authorities on Thursday that they were “canceling their participation” in the event, according to an official from the French space ministry. “Four American companies canceled their participation in the space summit today: Stoke Space, Starcloud, Blue Origin, and SpaceX," a ministry official told POLITICO. POLITICO first reported earlier this week that the White House put pressure on U.S. companies to boycott the summit. "It is hard not to draw a connection to the rumors of pressure that have been circulating in the press. We obviously want to continue working with our American partners and allies, even if strategic shifts and political pressures sometimes make the task unnecessarily complex!” the French official said in a text message, adding that other U.S. companies will participate. The summit, taking place on Sept. 9-10, is a key event for Macron. He is keen to ensure that France and Europe remain credible space powers, with an independent launch capability and their own global satellite communications system — avoiding being dependent on U.S. technology. The summit is expected to bring together delegations from the countries alongside space agencies, industry leaders, scientists and military officials. Advertisement Advertisement But the event comes at a time of strained relations between Europe and the U.S., including over space policy. Washington has lobbied against the European Commission’s EU Space Act, a proposed rulebook for space activities the U.S. sees as targeting American companies by imposing EU rules on them. A Franco-German push to allocate more mobile-satellite frequencies to European companies, including the EU’s IRIS² satellite network, is also angering the U.S. Brussels, Paris and Berlin do not want Europe’s satellite connectivity to depend entirely on Starlink or other U.S. providers. For Washington, however, it looks like another example of the EU using regulation and market access to build European champions at the expense of American companies. French authorities first tried to downplay the Trump administration’s summit threat, arguing U.S. companies were still welcome. Despite that effort, six French and space industry officials told POLITICO they were not surprised by what they describe as a classic Trump move. The U.S. administration has repeatedly tried to torpedo multilateral initiatives, ranging from global climate measures to quitting the World Health Organization, while also trying to block any European effort to reduce reliance on U.S. companies. “This is so typical of Trump,” said a space company official who will be participating in the summit. Like others in this story, they were granted anonymity to speak candidly. “Trump likes to belittle Europeans … and even more Macron, who somehow embodies European ‘leadership.’” Lackluster attendance by U.S. companies is a short-term blow to the summit and Macron. But several space and French officials stressed it will also energize European efforts to reduce reliance on the U.S. “The silver lining is we’re diversifying our partnerships around the world, investing in our own space industry. It’s not about uncoupling but looking at what we can do with other partners,” said a space official. Two space industry officials also told POLITICO that Trump’s boycott will have a limited impact. Even if the four companies skip next week’s summit, the World Space Business Week taking place a week later in Paris is set, for now, to include major American space companies like Starlink and Blue Origin. Advertisement Advertisement French officials also argue that any hole left by American businesses will be filled by others. “Is it really that big a deal if [American companies] aren’t there? That’s the question. Other powers will be there, particularly the Chinese,” one official said. Christophe Grudler, a French member of the European Parliament who worked on the EU Space Act, said: “If other players in the space sector adopt a more cooperative attitude, they’ll obviously score points. I’m not saying that’s a solution either, but the effect of Mr. Trump’s mood was that the Chinese or others would come across as more likable.” The Elysée and the French foreign ministry declined to comment. Clea Caulcutt and Audrey Decker contributed to this report. This article has been updated.

Photograph: Ben Birchall/PA England Woman’s world ‘tilted on axis’ on learning husband invited men to sexually assault her, court told Four men on trial charged with sexually assaulting Joanne Young while she was sedated, restrained and blindfolded Steven Morris Tue 27 Oct 2026 11.29 EDT Last modified on Tue 27 Oct 2026 12.52 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A woman’s world was “tilted on its axis” when she discovered that for years her former husband had been drugging her and inviting men into their family home to sexually assault her while she was restrained and blindfolded, a court has been told. Philip Young, 50, advertised his then wife, Joanne Young, on dating and swinging websites, presenting it as a “kink” for both of them, Winchester crown court heard. In fact, he had been sedating her, plunging her into “an inanimate state” where anything could be done to her by whoever answered the adverts, jurors were told. The businessman has pleaded guilty to multiple charges of abuse against his former wife, who has waived her right to anonymity. View image in fullscreen Philip Young. Photograph: Crown Prosecution Service/PA The jury of eight men and four women is hearing the trial of four men jointly charged with sexually assaulting Joanne Young, 49. The alleged assaults carried out by the four – Connor Sanderson-Doyle, 32, Richard Wilkins, 62, Norman Macksoni, 48, and Mohammed Hassan, 38 – are said to have taken place between the summer of 2016 and the winter of 2023. They deny the charges. Sarah Jones KC, prosecuting, said Joanne Young had no idea what had been happening to her when police arrived at the family home in Swindon, Wiltshire. She said: “The world she thought she knew had entirely tilted on its axis. The relationship she thought she had appears now to be wholly unreal – she does not even know what she doesn’t know.” Jones told jurors they were going to have to contend with “some depressingly awful and sordid material”. She told them: “You are going to see videos of things you cannot then un-see and may find you can’t forget.” Jones said the videos that formed the bulk of the evidence showed Joanne Young was the victim of her husband’s fantasy to watch her being “crawled over” by men “plucked from the internet”. The barrister said the case was about whether it was ever reasonable to have sex with an unknown woman without checking with her first. “Whether it is ever reasonable to think someone truly can give consent on another’s behalf,” she added. The barrister said the pair married in 2004 and had three children, now young adults. She said: “From the outside they seemed a normal couple with a normal family life.” Joanne Young characterised her sex life as “fairly normal” and was emphatic that she and her husband were “monogamous … physically and emotionally … the traditional sense of marriage … it was us two kind of till the end.” She didn’t like being out of control, not even liking to take a sleeping tablet, the prosecutor said. View image in fullscreen Joanne Young, who has waived her right to anonymity. Photograph: Wiltshire police/PA The court was told her husband had some “preferences” in their sex life, such as blindfolding and using restraints on his wife, which she did not object to. In 2015 a packet of a sedative drug that had been posted to Philip Young from India was intercepted at customs. Police visited him and he denied any knowledge of it, telling them someone must have obtained his name through his business. Jones said this helped build a picture of Young searching from 2015, at least, for drugs that could be used on their own or with alcohol to send Joanne Young into “a deep sleep where she would be disoriented, unaware of her surroundings and unlikely to be able to recall what happened”. In 2023, after a night out, Joanne Young had an indication that her marriage was not what she had believed, the jury heard. While she and her husband were having sex, she “felt someone else’s hand on my wrist and it wasn’t his [her husband’s] hand”. She said “I was obviously really shocked because, obviously you don’t expect someone else to be in your bedroom. Phil said to the person: ‘Get down’, and the person ducked at the end of the bed.” Joanne Young later said: “I was just really shocked. There was this man in my house and I was naked.” She hid in the bathroom. The following morning Young said he had been looking in “forums” and invited someone round the house to watch them have sex. Jones said: “She had stumbled upon the edges of a far greater issue in her relationship. Young had advertised her on websites – he sought strangers to come and sleep with his wife – any age, any race – but as close to Swindon as possible so that when the circumstances were right they could be seized upon immediately.” The investigation began when police received a notification that the user of a social media account connected to Philip Young had uploaded extreme pornography. Officers went to his address and found videos of Joanne Young lying naked on her bed, restrained and blindfolded while other men engaged in sexual activity with her as her husband recorded what had taken place. Jones told the jury that none of the defendants now suggested Joanne Young was actually consenting. She said: “Each agrees that she was not. But what each defendant is likely to say is that they believed at the time that she was consenting, and to argue that such a belief was reasonable.” The prosecutor continued: “It is their last desperate throw of the dice to convince certainly you and perhaps even themselves that they are not rapists or sexual offenders when they took what her husband was offering out to them without ever checking for a second with the woman herself whether she was OK with it.” Young will be sentenced after this trial.
